original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) was performed on a Biacore T200 instrument (GE Healthcare) using a CM5 sensor chip. The SmVKR2KD protein was immobilized on the chip via amine coupling. The immobilization was performed at pH 4.0 using 100 mM sodium acetate buffer. The protein was captured at a flow rate of 5 μL/min. The immobilized protein was then blocked with 1 M ethanolamine, pH 8.5. The SPR experiments were performed in HBS-EP buffer (10 mM HEPES, 150 mM NaCl, 3 mM EDTA, 0.005% P20, pH 7.4) at 25 °C. The compounds were diluted in the running buffer and injected at a flow rate of 30 μL/min for 120 s, followed by a dissociation phase of 120 s. The reference surface was regenerated with 10 mM glycine-HCl, pH 2.0, for 30 s. The data were analyzed using Biacore T200 evaluation software. The binding affinity (KD) was determined by fitting the sensorgrams to a 1:1 Langmuir binding model. The SPR experiments were performed in triplicate.
original_paragraph.Figure 1 caption: Figure 1. Changes in the average motility of adult S. mansoni as a function of time, as measured by WormAssay. Significance was determined by Student’s t-test (two-tailed): *P < 0.05, **P < 0.005, ***P < 0.0005. Data were derived from three to five biological assays with 10 μM compound.

Compounds in black do not have a common substructure.
original_paragraph.Results section: We employed surface plasmon resonance (SPR) to screen the PKIS2 library against the SmVKR2KD. The PKIS2 library comprises 645 small molecule inhibitors representing 86 diverse chemotypes.25 Twelve showed the strongest binding to the SmVKR2KD with affinities between 0.57 and 170 μM (Table 1 and Figure S3). The identified inhibitors display a similar backbone consisting of either a 1H-pyrrolo[2,3-b]pyridine linked to benzene or a pyrimidine linked to benzene or pyrazolo[1,5-b]pyridazine (Table 1). GSK1520489 and GSK986310 had the highest affinities of 0.44 μM and 1.96 μM, respectively. Both compounds contain a 2,4-diaminopyrimidine as the putative hinge-binding moiety that likely drives binding.
